traceability.notes:
Assessment for Story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md (Requirement Content Validation):
1) Core Functionality - Implemented by ESLint rule src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts. - For @story + @req: - The rule tracks the most recent @story path in a file and validates every subsequent @req line against that story. - It loads the story file, extracts all requirement IDs matching /REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g, and checks that each referenced reqId from @req is present. - For @supports: - Each @supports line provides its own story path and one or more requirement IDs. - The rule resolves that path, loads and parses the story file once (cached), and validates each reqId. - Tests in tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts explicitly cover both valid and invalid scenarios, including missing requirements and ensure the correct ESLint messages are emitted. - Result: The plugin does validate that @req (and @supports) annotations reference requirements actually present in the target story files. Core functionality is satisfied.
2) Quality Standards (various formats and story structures) - Requirement IDs are discovered via a simple but effective regex (/REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g) over the entire markdown file content. This is agnostic to markdown structure, so it works for: - Inline requirements in text - Bullet list requirements (validated via tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md and corresponding tests) - Numbered lists or acceptance criteria where IDs appear anywhere in the line - Multi-story scenarios are validated through @supports handling using fixtures story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md, proving support for: - Shared IDs across different files (scoped per story) - Multiple requirement IDs per annotation line. - Because the rule does not depend on specific markdown section headings, it naturally handles requirements located in different sections (Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, etc.) as long as they contain REQ- identifiers. - Result: Deep validation handles multiple requirement formats and story file structures consistent with the story (IDs can appear in bullets, text, multiple files). This acceptance criterion is reasonably met.
3) Integration with existing validation and parsing logic - Rule is integrated into the plugin’s dynamic rule loading and flat-config presets via src/index.ts: - Included in RULE_NAMES and dynamically required as ./rules/valid-req-reference. - Mapped to error severity in TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES. - Present in both recommended and strict configs. - It operates on the same annotation conventions used by other rules (valid-annotation-format, valid-story-reference, require-*-annotation rules), and tests demonstrate coexistence without conflicts. - It reuses the same conceptual model of @story/@req annotations and adds deep content validation on top; existing rules can still enforce structural correctness and file existence, while this rule enforces requirement-level existence. - Result: Integration criterion is met.
4) User Experience (clear error messages) - ESLint messages: - reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'" - Tests assert both messageId and associated data (reqId, storyPath), ensuring that when a requirement is missing, the developer sees exactly which ID and which story path are involved. - The documentation file docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md explains these behaviors and shows example violations. - Result: User experience criterion is clearly satisfied.
5) Error Handling (malformed files, missing sections, parsing issues) - loadAndCacheRequirements() wraps file reading in a try/catch: - On read error (e.g., missing file, permission issues), it caches an empty Set instead of throwing, preventing ESLint from crashing. - Subsequent validations against that file will see no requirements and emit reqMissing for referenced IDs, which is graceful from a linting perspective. - Because requirement extraction is regex-based, malformed markdown or unusual structure does not cause parsing errors; it simply results in fewer or no matches. - validateAndResolveStoryPath() prevents unsafe paths (.., absolute paths, leaving project root) and reports invalidPath rather than failing the analysis. - Combined, this means malformed or unreadable story files do not break the rule; they lead to diagnostic messages instead of runtime errors. - Result: Error handling criterion is satisfied at the intended level of robustness (no crashes, clear diagnostics for bad paths and missing IDs).
6) Documentation - docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md exists and is directly tied to this story via @story and REQ-DEEP-* annotations. - It describes: - What the rule does (deep validation of @req and @supports against story content). - How paths are validated and what errors are reported. - How requirement IDs are scoped per story file. - Concrete examples for correct and incorrect usages, including single-story, multi-story, missing requirements, and path issues. - It also explains the interaction between @story/@req and @supports annotations and references the multi-story support story for further context. - Result: Documentation acceptance criterion is fully met.
7) Requirement-level mapping - REQ-DEEP-PARSE: Implemented via extractStoryPath, extractReqIdFromLine, loadAndCacheRequirements, processCommentLines, and processAllComments; tests cover valid parsing from in-file annotations and story fixtures. - REQ-DEEP-MATCH: Implemented via checkRequirementExists and its integration in validateReqLine and validateImplementsLine; tests explicitly exercise missing-requirement scenarios for both @req and @supports. - REQ-DEEP-FORMAT: Different placement formats (inline, bullets, multiple stories) are supported because IDs are matched anywhere in the markdown text via regex; bullet and multi-story fixture tests verify this. - REQ-DEEP-SECTION: Because parsing is global and section-agnostic, requirements in any markdown section are naturally discovered; there is no section-specific limitation. - REQ-DEEP-CACHE: Implemented by the reqCache Map keyed by resolvedStoryPath, populated once per file per Program run and reused for all validations in that run. - REQ-DEEP-ERROR: Implemented via reqMissing and invalidPath messages with specific data; tests assert correct messageId and data for error scenarios.
Conclusion: The deep validation functionality described in docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md is fully implemented, integrated, tested, and documented. All acceptance criteria and listed requirements are met based on concrete code, tests, and documentation evidence. Therefore, this story is assessed as PASSED.
